🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Steve Ellis, the English singer best known as the frontman of the 1960s pop group Love Affair and the voice of its chart-topping hit "Everlasting Love," has died at 76.

His death was confirmed on his official Facebook account on November 1, 2026. The statement said: "After complications from a chronic illness, Steve peacefully left the world on the evening of October 30, 2026, in the presence of his loved ones." No more specific cause of death has been publicly disclosed.

Ellis was born Stephen John Ellis on April 7, 1950, in Edgware, north London. He was still a teenager when Love Affair, formed from the Soul Survivors in 1966, released "Everlasting Love" in December 1967. The song reached No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart in early 1968, displacing The Beatles' "Hello, Goodbye" from the top spot, when Ellis was just 17.

"Everlasting Love" remained Ellis's signature song for the rest of his life, and it later appeared in films including Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason and Belfast. After Love Affair, he went on to front the hard-rock group Widowmaker and the band Ellis, and he continued performing and recording for decades, releasing a new album in 2026.

Tributes followed the announcement from longtime friend and songwriter David Courtney, who shared news of Ellis's passing, as well as from Boom Radio and Heritage Chart Radio, which remembered him as one of British music's great soul voices.

Rest in Peace, Steve Ellis.

Sources: Official Facebook statement; Clash Music; The Sun; Beat Magazine.
